title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1967-01-27

ai_review.summary: Rough hand‑held mono cassette recording of a raw 1967 show, but the performance shines with blistering Viola Lee Blues, New Potato Caboose and Alligator>Caution.
ai_review.review: The tape is an audience capture on a cheap mono cassette – muddy, low‑fidelity and riddled with drop‑outs – yet listeners repeatedly note that the music more than compensates.  Highlights include a ferocious Viola Lee Blues, a soaring New Potato Caboose, the Alligator>Caution marathon and Pigpen’s dominant organ work; Jerry’s solos are described as fiery and intense.  Expect a historic snapshot of early‑67 Dead energy rather than pristine sound.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviewers give 4–5 stars for the musical performance despite repeated complaints about the recording quality; the show is consistently praised while the technical side is rated poor, yielding a high overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hand‑held mono cassette capture; very low fidelity, muddy mids, occasional drop‑outs and limited stereo image.  Some tracks (Viola Lee) are more listenable than others, but overall the tape is described as almost unlistenable for modern ears.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑67 Dead set – raw, improvisational and organ‑forward.  The band rides long jams (Alligator>Caution) and delivers high‑energy blues numbers; the pacing is loose but exhilarating for fans of the pre‑album era.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as fiery with intense solos on Viola Lee Blues and Morning Dew; his tone is praised despite the lo‑fi recording.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work is repeatedly highlighted as a centerpiece of the show, often described as “swirling” and “dominant”.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (and occasionally Mickey) are noted as low in the mix; some reviewers mention a drum intro on Alligator>Caution.
